why: A = exists_scComplement_le ∧ isGeneralPositionRetractAt_of_sup_eq_top: general sc-linear algebra (any finite-dimensional smooth N, any sc-subspace TR, M = N + TR) and its chart form for an arbitrary sc-retract Q ⊆ R.retract, R tame for T, at a smooth level-1 point y with T_yQ + E_0 = E. B is the instance in an M-polyfold chart: Q = φ(A ∩ V) for a smooth submanifold with data (V, s), V ⊆ dom φ, the model a tame retract, plus the two submodule equalities M = N + (E_0 ∩ M) = N + T^R_zO. A ⇒ B is glue: the data gives the sc⁺ chart retraction t onto φ(A ∩ V) (exists_chartRetraction; W = V since V ⊆ dom φ), so N = range Dt(z) is finite-dimensional and smooth (Lemma 4.7) and z is smooth; IsTameRetract's tame R is tame for the given T; the sc-complement B' ⊆ M ∩ E_z comes from A, and the equalities follow from M = N ⊕ B' by the modular law. B ⇒ A fails genuinely: A holds for arbitrary sc-retracts Q (not images of sc⁺-retractions) and arbitrary N, TR, which B does not cover.
